source_review.notes: Checked current official FOCUS split-allocation requirements, FinOps allocation guidance, OpenCost specification, Kubernetes quota/multi-tenancy/scheduling documentation, and AWS, Google Cloud, and Microsoft billing/allocation/alert documentation. All thirteen final references returned HTTP 200. Provider timing and control behavior is attributed.

evidence: Reviewed authoritative, direct, shared, idle, unresolved, origin-charge, driver, allocation-ratio, useful-output, unit-cost, coverage, budget, quota, and priority notation.
Checked monetary conservation, nonnegative driver ratios, zero-denominator handling, boundary-aligned division, and currency/time-period requirements.
Checked that billed, effective, amortized, marginal, and list costs plus physical/logical units remain distinct.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Allocation is explicitly a versioned policy applied to reconciled source measures rather than a claim of uniquely discovered causality.

evidence: Executed the Python 3 fixture and reproduced a 9,000.00 shared charge after 2,000.00 and 1,000.00 direct charges from a 12,000.00 total.
Recomputed 6,000:3,000 driver allocation as 6,000.00 and 3,000.00 shared, yielding 8,000.00 and 4,000.00 workload totals that reconcile to 12,000.00.
Recomputed unit costs as 100.00 and 200.00 currency units per million correct records for 80-million and 20-million outputs.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The fixture proves arithmetic and conservation only; real allocations also require valid identity, time overlap, source reconciliation, pricing policy, causal drivers, and correct denominators.

evidence: Verified total cost partitions into direct workload allocations, shared workload allocations, explicit idle, and unresolved cost.
Verified nonnegative workload driver ratios sum to one for a positive denominator and therefore conserve each shared origin charge.
Verified unit cost divides reconciled workload cost by correct useful output over the same boundary while failed/retried work remains in cost.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: A zero driver denominator is intentionally retained as idle/unallocated or handled by an explicit policy, never divided or silently discarded.

evidence: Reviewed zero total/output/driver, negative credits, currency conversion, rounding, late charges, invoice corrections, commitment underuse, taxes, and restatements.
Reviewed missing/stale/mutated tags, concurrent shared executors, retries/speculation, autoscaling, asynchronous storage/network charges, and ownership changes.
Reviewed delayed alerts, runaway requests, hard stops, stateful commits, recovery reserve, preemption, backfill retries, quota contention, gaming, and sensitive metadata.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Shared, idle, unresolved, failed-attempt, central-platform, and consumer-attributed costs remain visible rather than being forced into false precision.

evidence: Traced provider origin records through reconciliation, temporal identity enrichment, one-winner direct matching, shared allocation, residue, and restatement.
Checked workload identity across execution, task attempts, speculative losers, shared nodes, storage prefixes, requests, durable outputs, and useful-output validation.
Checked governance actions against service class, capacity, critical sections, state/commit/recovery status, protected reserve, exception, and audit requirements.
invariant_checking.notes: Allocated records preserve origin, method, driver quantities, ratio, policy version, and reconstructability within disclosed tolerance.

evidence: Reviewed cost-conservation proof across direct, allocated shared, idle, and unresolved partitions.
Reviewed driver-ratio proof and the necessity of explicit zero-denominator behavior.
Reviewed unit-cost correctness gate and temporal-overlap obligation for historical ownership.
proof_review.notes: Conservation proves arithmetic completeness, not fairness or causal quality; those depend on documented drivers and the decision context.

evidence: Audited billing/effective/direct/shared/idle cost, allocation driver, showback, chargeback, unit cost, coverage, budget, quota, governance, and conservation terms.
Confirmed requested versus used allocation, shared versus idle ownership, coverage versus attribution quality, and policy movement versus physical efficiency are distinct.
Confirmed budgets are described as delayed planning/alert boundaries unless a separate runtime enforcement mechanism exists.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Cost controls are conditioned on correctness, reliability, security, retention, and recovery rather than treated as unconditional optimization.

evidence: Reviewed invoice/export costs, credits/corrections, CPU/memory/GPU time, byte-time, requests, transfers, attempts, output, idle, commitments, and allocation residue.
Reviewed segmentation by invoice/account/currency/period, provider/service/SKU/resource/region, owner/product/environment/pipeline/execution/attempt, and policy version.
Confirmed coverage, unresolved causes, tag freshness, driver values, denominator quality, budget latency, quota/admission/preemption events, and exceptions remain observable.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Tags, list prices, node wall time, or 100% forced allocation are not mislabeled as complete workload-cost evidence.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed cost purposes/measures, authoritative ledgers, stable workload identity, direct/shared resource allocation, idle/commitments, conservation, unit economics, change decomposition, showback/chargeback, governance, budgets, background work, gaming, and policy lifecycle.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable temporal identities, one-winner rules, per-resource drivers, origin reconstruction, dispute drill-down, delayed-versus-runtime controls, protected service classes, exception expiry, dual-run policy changes, and monthly reconciliation. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from cost vocabulary/conservation through workload identity, causal allocation, unit economics, and safe governance. Ten examples and five answered exercises cover shared splits, reconciliation, idle, retries, temporal tags, quotas, delayed alerts, ledgers, drivers, budgets, and chargeback.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external FOCUS/FinOps/OpenCost/Kubernetes/AWS/Google/Microsoft maintainer, accountant/auditor/finance/tax/procurement/FinOps/runtime/storage/network/platform/SRE/security/privacy specialist, production operator, workload owner, affected user, governance or accessibility specialist, or certification review is claimed.
